header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (XyloTech Head of ML), Luca Rinaldi (XyloTech Platform Eng), Ana Torres (XyloTech Data Ops), Tom Briggs (XyloTech PM)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood's Eval/Quality monitoring: building prompt-sets, configuring regression alerts, running A/B traffic splits and interpreting AB compare results. Customer interested in pilot for support docs summarization product; concerns: latency impact, cost of continuous eval, and SSO/KMS requirements.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me?
[00:02] Maya: yep loud and clear, thanks for doing this.
[00:05] Jon: hi all, i'll be demoing the eval console and AB compare flows, i might jump into the console in a bit.
[00:10] Tom: quick agenda from our side, we want to see how prompt sets map to alerts, how the regression signal is computed, and what it looks like to do traffic splits across model variants.
[00:22] Samira: perfect, we'll start high level then do a live prompt-set import. also happy to cover security questions at the end.
[00:30] Jon: (screen) ok opening the EvalOps console, top-left is Prompt Sets, you can upload CSVs or create programmatically via API. a prompt-set is just a labeled set of inputs + expected outputs or metrics.
[00:47] Ana: when you say expected outputs, is that strict matching or can it be scorer-based?
[00:52] Jon: good question. we support both exact match labels and scorer functions — you can use a rubric, or a reranker, or an automated metric like BERTScore. you can chain metrics.
[01:05] Luca: is the scorer executed in Redwood or do we call our own evaluation endpoint?
[01:10] Jon: by default Redwood will compute builtin metrics on the server side; for custom scoring you can attach a webhook to forward outputs to your scoring service and we ingest the result, so either works.
[01:22] Maya: lets say we have 500 prompts from our support transcripts, we want to run nightly regressions and alert if doc-summa F1 drops by more than 3 points — easy?
[01:30] Jon: totally. in the Alerts tab you create a regression alert, pick the metric (F1), set the baseline (last 30 days median), and threshold — we compute significance with bootstrap so you won't get noisy ticks.
[01:45] Tom: is the baseline configurable per prompt subset? we have high-priority prompt categories vs low priority.
[01:50] Jon: yes you can tag prompts and create alerts scoped to tags or a prompt-set. tags also let you create tiered paging rules.
[01:58] Maya: ok nice. Priya: on the product side, how is the AB compare surfaced?
[02:02] Priya: we show side-by-side metric deltas and per-prompt diffs, plus a waterfall to see which prompts drive the regression. you can filter by label or by model variant.
[02:15] Jon: launching AB compare demo — starting traffic-split wizard. you can route percentage to a stable vs candidate model, or route by user cohort.
[02:28] Luca: we need traffic-split that honors region and data residency, can we restrict candidate only to EU region instances?
[02:36] Samira: yes, in Private/Dedicated you can pin model variants to regions, routing policies can include region constraints. if you're on hosted we'd recommend model variants with region affinity; for strict residency we'd look at Private.
[02:50] Maya: how about costs — continuous nightly evals for 500 prompts across multiple models, is that going to be expensive?
[02:58] Jon: cost depends on token counts and whether you run full inference or use cached outputs. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching so for many support prompts with similar prefixes, cost reduces. also Optimize suggests batching and quant profiles to drop per-token cost.
[03:15] Tom: can we do lightweight sentinel checks daily and full eval weekly?
[03:18] Jon: yes, you can schedule multiple eval jobs with different coverage; alerts can be tied to either. common pattern we see: cheap sentinel alerts (10–20 prompts) daily + full smoke test (500 prompts) weekly.
[03:33] Maya: show us an example where an A/B compare highlighted a regression and we rolled back automatically.
[03:38] Jon: flipping to a case study — here's an ecom customer: candidate model introduced hallucination on price answers, AB compare showed a 7% precision drop on price-extraction prompts, we had an automatic fallback policy that rolled traffic back to stable and created a ticket.
[03:55] Ana: what triggered the rollback, the alert or manual?
[03:58] Jon: both possible — you can configure an automatic action on critical alerts; most teams prefer manual review with auto-flagging.
[04:07] Maya: about integrations — we use SSO with Okta and KMS via AWS, any blockers?
[04:12] Samira: we support SAML/Okta SSO and KMS integration for Private; in Hosted we offer managed encryption at rest and KMS-handoff options for enterprise.
[04:24] Luca: audit logs required for our compliance team — can we store full evaluation logs for 365 days?
[04:30] Samira: yes with the enterprise observability add-on you can retain logs and we provide per-token breakdowns, user-level access controls and exportable audit trails.
[04:40] Tom: question on latency impact — running evals shouldn't slow production, right?
[04:44] Jon: evals run asynchronously on separate pools by default; A/B traffic splits are real-time but you can route evaluation-only traffic to dedicated inference workers. important design: don't route control-plane evals through your production path.
[04:58] Maya: ok demo to import a prompt-set — (typing noise) uploading CSV now — mapping columns: id, prompt, expected_label, tags.
[05:10] Jon: we detect columns and let you preview. note: try to avoid long context fields in CSV; heavy tokens blow up cost.
[05:20] Ana: oops one of our expected labels had markdown, it got sanitized — is that normal?
[05:25] Jon: the parser will escape common markup; you can set a raw_text flag if you want literal processing.
[05:33] Samira: quick interjection, if you want we'll share the sample prompt-set format and a tiny ingestion lambda that our customers use.
[05:38] Maya: please do.
[05:40] Jon: running an on-demand eval job — selecting models: stable-v1 (quantized) vs candidate-ptx (float). submitting job... job queued.
[05:55] (pause, typing)
[06:10] Jon: results streaming — per-prompt diffs show candidate worse on 12 prompts, combined metric delta -2.9 F1.
[06:20] Tom: can the console show the original model output next to candidate output?
[06:23] Jon: yes side-by-side with diff highlights and token-level alignment when available.
[06:30] Maya: the per-prompt view is great. can we add comments for the team?
[06:33] Jon: yep annotate and assign to reviewers; annotations get surfaced in the eval timeline.
[06:40] Priya: want to call out the regression alert config UI — here you can tweak sensitivity, minimum sample size and who gets paged.
[06:50] Ana: paging — we use PagerDuty.
[06:52] Samira: Redwood integrates with PD, Slack, e-mail and Jira. you can route alerts to different PD services per prompt tag.
[07:00] Maya: what about model rollouts — can we do gradual canary and auto-promote if metrics look good?
[07:05] Jon: yes rollout policies include canary stages, metric gates and auto-promote after X hours with stable deltas. you can tie gates to eval metrics in real-time.
[07:15] Luca: curious about private deployment — if we want to keep everything in our VPC and run evals there, is that supported?
[07:20] Samira: yes Private installs include EvalOps console; metrics and dashboards can be run on-prem and we provide a private control plane option. you can also bring-your-own-KMS and SSO.
[07:32] Maya: any prebuilt connectors for Salesforce/Intercom to pull prompts?
[07:36] Jon: we have connectors for Zendesk, Intercom, and a REST ingestion endpoint. many customers use small ETL jobs to export recent conversations into prompt-sets.
[07:48] Tom: ok pricing ask: rough estimate for 100k eval tokens/week across two model variants and nightly sentinel checks?
[07:56] Samira: i'll need to run numbers but rough ballpark on hosted with caching and batching we usually see X per 1k tokens — (Samira clarifies) i'll send a modeled estimate in the follow up.
[08:10] Maya: any hard limits on prompt-set size?
[08:13] Jon: not really; console pages results and we recommend slicing into sets > 10k for runs, but you can store millions with enterprise retention.
[08:22] Ana: transcription note: the automated speaker tags sometimes flip for us, just FYI.
[08:26] Samira: yep that's expected, we'll correct in notes.
[08:30] (wrap)
[08:31] Samira: ok quick recap of next steps, we'll send the security snippet, sample prompt-set, cost estimate and propose a pilot date.
[08:40] Maya: thanks — we'll reconvene once we pick pilot cohort.
[08:44] Jon: thanks all, follow up will include exported screenshots of the AB compare and the webhook example.
[08:50] (call ends)
notes: Customer is piloting a support doc summarization feature; primary metrics: F1 on extraction, hallucination rate, latency. Strong interest in private deployment for residency and KMS. Preferred pilot: 4-week with nightly sentinel + weekly full eval and AB split for candidate model.
